newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds end mixed on good volume.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds end mixed on good volume.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds ended mixed on Tuesday after substantial trading pushed long-term investment-grade bonds lower and helped junk bonds extend their recent gains, traders said.
Some traders said a heavy forward calendar of new supply was triggering some selling of long-term high-grade bonds as money managers adjusted their portfolios.

But others said a flat yield curve that did not compensate managers for investing in long-maturity bonds, was the source of the pressure. They added most of the new supply will have intermediate maturities and will not affect the long end.
Spreads on long-term investment grade bonds ended the day unchanged to several basis points wider, traders said.
High-yield bonds may have benefitted from exactly the opposite conditions from those in the investment-grade market.
One trader said a lack of new high-yield issues this week was triggering buying in the secondary market.
"Fund managers still have a lot of cash and with no new issues coming, they're buying secondary paper," he said.
High-yield bonds ended the day unchanged to 1/4 a point higher on substantial volume, traders reported.

In credit-specific news, Viacom Inc debt ended the day over five basis points wider on news that the company planned to sell a minority interest in its Blockbuster Entertainment chain of video stores in a public offering.
The spread on Viacom ten-year debt tightened to 175 basis points from 181 basis points when the company initially announced that proceeds from the offering would be used to repay debt, traders said.
But the spread reversed direction, widening to 187 basis points over Treasuries after news of Blockbuster's poor recent results was fully digested, traders said.
"When people realized that (Viacom) stock was off more than five points, they started to get more concerned about what exactly the company will do in the future," said one trader.
Market participants also viewed with concern the resignation of Bill Fields, the respected chairman and chief executive of Blockbuster, traders said.
In the high-yield market, traders reported better buying of radio company credits. Prices in the radio sector have recently been depressed, they said.

Sterling Chemicals Holdings Inc's senior subordinated notes surged four points, while its zero coupon bonds rose two points, a trader said. He was unaware of a specific event which triggered the price increases.

In the Treasury market, the price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 18/32 to 94-26/32, pushing the yield down to 7.04 percent. The price of the 10-year Treasury rose 8/32 to 95-28/32, pushing the yield down to 6.83 percent.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 173.38, its second largest advance in history.
